questions.q: What do you usually have for breakfast?
questions.answer: Usually something simple, like paratha with egg or a bit of vegetable curry, along with a cup of tea. It's not elaborate, but it's [[wholesome]] and keeps me going until lunch.

questions.q: What is your favourite meal of the day?
questions.answer: Definitely dinner. It's the one meal where the whole family sits down together and actually talks, so it's as much about the company as the food. It's become a small daily [[ritual]] I really value.

questions.q: Do you prefer eating at home or in restaurants?
questions.answer: Mostly at home, to be honest. Home-cooked food is healthier and more comforting. That said, I do enjoy dining out now and then, especially when it's a chance to [[socialise]] with friends over a meal.

questions.q: Is there a traditional dish from your country you'd recommend?
questions.answer: I'd definitely recommend hilsa fish, especially cooked in mustard sauce. It's our national fish, and it has a rich, [[distinctive]] flavour. During Pohela Boishakh, many families eat it with panta bhat.

questions.q: Have your eating habits changed in recent years?
questions.answer: Somewhat, yes. I used to eat a lot of fried street food, but now I try to cut back on oily snacks and eat more vegetables. I haven't given them up completely, but I'm certainly more [[health-conscious]] than before.
